mechanism_narrative: The sharp rise in PARKS mobility over the latest week signals warmer-weather discretionary outings that spill into nearby shopping and dining trips, raising RETAIL_REC within four weeks if PARKS stays near zero or positive after a deep negative trough.
failure_condition: If PARKS falls back below -15 for two consecutive weeks and RETAIL_REC still rises over the next 28 days, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above +7 while WORKPLACES stays below -30, households substitute local shopping for commuting-oriented spending, so RETAIL_REC increases over the next two weeks as people consolidate errands near home.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above +7 and WORKPLACES stays below -30 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not improve versus the prior four weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A continued easing in TRANSIT mobility indicates fewer constraints on cross-city movement; once TRANSIT recovers by at least 3 points from its recent level, retail trips follow with a short lag and RETAIL_REC rises within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points from the prior week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT improves by 3 or more points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC does not improve in the same or following week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A near-zero PARKS reading after prior weakness marks an early seasonal shift that precedes broader leisure spending, so RETAIL_REC rises over four weeks only if PARKS remains above -5 for at least two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS stays above -5 for two straight weeks but RETAIL_REC remains below its last-four-week mean, the seasonal mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC move together, household errand bundling is strengthening: more shopping visits combine essentials with discretionary purchases, pushing RETAIL_REC upward over the next two weeks when grocery mobility is also recovering from its recent low.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises for two consecutive weeks after a monthly decline
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises for two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not rise in the same two-week window, the bundling hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility reflects time spent near home and neighborhood-based consumption; when RESIDENTIAL stays above +7 without a matching rebound in WORKPLACES, RETAIL_REC drifts higher over the next four weeks through local convenience trips.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above +7 while WORKPLACES stays below -30 and RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates relaxation of movement limits and fuller in-person activity; this combined recovery lifts retail visits within four weeks, but only after both series turn up together from their current depressed levels.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise week-on-week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve for two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior four-week average, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS from a deep trough signals favorable weather and higher weekend foot traffic, but the effect on RETAIL_REC appears only over one week when PARKS jumps from strongly negative toward zero; otherwise retail remains flat.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by at least 15 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If PARKS rises by 15 or more points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC does not improve within the next week, the hypothesis is rejected.
